author: Elaine Kwon

author: Elaine Kwon

author: Jordan Taylor

author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Zalando expects much slower growth in 2022 as European shoppers turn cautious. Partner brands should plan conservatively and supply what Zalando needs.

author: Jordan Taylor

author: Elaine Kwon

desc: Mother’s Day gift shoppers buy late and care most about arrival. In 2022, marketplace sellers win by promising May 8 delivery and making gifts easy to choose.

author: Jordan Taylor

author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Amazon runs the marketplace brands sell on and competes with them through its own retail and brands. Congress is debating limits. Plan for both roles.

author: Jordan Taylor

author: Elaine Kwon

title: Amazon DSP in 2022 earns its budget only when lift is measured
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon DSP’s reported returns credit sales that would have happened anyway, most of all in retargeting. Fund it in 2022 on lift measured with a holdout.

title: Vendor Central in 2022 trades control for scale on Amazon’s terms
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Third-party sellers sold 56% of Amazon’s units in late 2021. Vendor Central still offers scale, but brands should plan for Amazon setting the terms.

title: The true cost of competing on Amazon is about a third of sales
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon’s fees, fulfillment and ads took an estimated 34% of seller revenue in 2021. Model the full cost of each unit sold, not the 15% referral fee.

title: Instagram shopping in 2022 is built for discovery, not checkout
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Instagram left shopping off its 2022 priorities in favor of video and creators. Brands should use it to be discovered and close sales where they convert best.

title: Roundel in 2022 pays off most for brands Target already stocks
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Roundel measures ads against Target’s own sales, in stores and online, so its return tracks a brand’s Target distribution. Size the budget to the shelf.

title: Walmart’s ad growth shows it wants ads in every supplier plan
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Walmart books part of its $2.1 billion ad business the way it books supplier funding. Plan Walmart Connect with your buyer, not as a separate e-commerce budget.

title: Why one-size-fits-all promotions stopped working
author: Jordan Taylor

title: Mercado Libre in 2022 rewards brands that use its logistics

title: Target Plus in 2022: who is getting invited, and why
author: Elaine Kwon

title: Amazon’s 2022 fee changes: model them before they hit margins

desc: Amazon’s average FBA fee rise of 5.2% hides a wide spread by size and weight. Model each product before January 18, then absorb, reprice or redesign.

title: Reading ROAS when prices rise: why the ratio flatters

title: Zalando’s logistics network is built for speed across Europe

title: Why absolute price means little in the Amazon Buy Box
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: The lowest sticker price does not reliably win the Amazon Buy Box. Fulfillment, delivery and seller record weigh as much, so compete on the whole offer.

title: The year in marketplaces, 2021: the structural shifts
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: In 2021, marketplaces earned more from ads, logistics and membership than from listings. Plan for platforms that sell services, not shelf space.

title: The 2022 e-commerce plan: four assumptions to change from 2021
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Four planning assumptions broke in 2021: the peak, ad costs, stock and measurement. A 2022 plan copied from 2021 carries every one of them forward.

title: Cyber Week 2021 lessons: how retailers and brands behaved
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Cyber Week 2021 showed retailers using deals to build memberships and brands discounting less. Plan 2022 around how they behave, not past peaks.

title: Cyber Week 2021 results, measured against the forecast
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Cyber Week 2021 came in below forecast, but November as a whole grew. Judge results against the season and your planning ranges, not the peak days.

title: How Zalando localized across Europe, and what brands should copy
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Zalando entered six European markets in 2021 with local assortments, payments and marketing. Brands selling there should localize just as deliberately.

title: Is Target Plus cannibalizing your direct sales?
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Brands worry that Target Plus takes sales from their own site. Some overlap is real, but it can be measured through new customers, site trends and price.

title: Early read: Black Friday 2021 online sales slip as the season spreads out
author: Kwontified
desc: Online spending on Black Friday, November 26, 2021, fell to $8.9 billion from about $9 billion a year earlier, the first time Adobe has recorded a…

title: Mercado Libre’s push into grocery opens a door for CPG brands
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Mercado Libre is building a supermarket business, and its grocery shoppers buy more often. CPG brands should test it with a focused, well-stocked range.

title: Paid and organic growth on Amazon need each other
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon ad costs keep rising, and paid growth alone gets more expensive. Brands should balance ad spend with the listings, reviews and stock behind it.

title: Walmart’s in-store returns change the economics of selling online
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Walmart made returns fast and free using its stores and FedEx. That raises shopper expectations, and marketplace sellers pay to meet them online.

title: How Buy Box changes quietly drain profit on Amazon
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: When a brand loses the Amazon Buy Box, sales and ad results fall, and teams often blame advertising. Track Buy Box share weekly to find the real cause.

title: Amazon sets a 48-hour Black Friday event for November 25 and 26
author: Kwontified
desc: On November 15, 2021, Amazon announced that more Black Friday deals than ever before will be available during a 48-hour event starting on Thursday…

title: A Target Plus operations checklist for the holiday season
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Target Plus sellers ship their own orders into a store-fulfilled retailer. A holiday checklist covers stock, shipping, pricing, returns and service.

title: Walmart store fulfillment turns store stock into online stock
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Walmart fulfills many online orders from its stores, so store stock is online stock. Brands should plan inventory, content and promotions around that.

title: What Amazon Ads unBoxed 2021 changes for advertisers
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: The headline at unBoxed 2021 was ads on Twitch, but the real change is measurement. Brands should set Brand Metrics baselines before 2022 budgets.

title: Facebook renames its parent company Meta
author: Kwontified
desc: On October 28, 2021, at its Connect conference, Facebook announced that its parent company is now called Meta, bringing its apps and technologies under…

title: Mercado Libre co-op marketing should buy data, not discounts
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Co-op marketing with Mercado Libre can build a brand’s presence across Latin America. It pays when brands negotiate for placement, data and measurement.

title: Amazon Ads unBoxed 2021: the announcements that matter for brands
author: Kwontified
desc: On October 26, 2021, the first day of its virtual unBoxed conference, Amazon Ads announced eight advertising and measurement solutions, including a new…

title: Amazon Accelerate 2021 pays brands to send customers to Amazon
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon’s Accelerate 2021 tools give brands more data and new ways to reach shoppers, but they also pay brands to send their own demand to Amazon. Weigh both.

title: Amazon Accelerate 2021: the announcements that matter for brands
author: Kwontified
desc: At its Accelerate 2021 conference for third-party sellers on October 20, 2021, Amazon announced new tools for product research and brand building, and…

title: Walmart’s rural advantage is its store network, not its website
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Walmart’s edge with rural shoppers comes from stores close to almost everyone. Brands should plan for shoppers who buy online and collect locally.

title: Q3 2021 Amazon Sponsored Ads benchmark: conversion up, ROAS down
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Q3 2021 Amazon ad results look weak next to a Prime Day quarter. Year over year, shoppers converted better, but returns slipped as clicks cost more.

title: Cyber Week 2021 planning needs one owner and an earlier calendar
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: With holiday deals starting in early October, Cyber Week 2021 runs the planning calendar. Brands need one owner who decides which deals to run and when.

title: Zalando returns are partly a brand problem, and partly fixable
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: About half of what Zalando sells comes back, and a third of returns are about size. Brands that improve their size data and content can cut that share.

title: Target Plus fulfillment works without Target’s stores
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Target’s stores fulfill nearly all its sales, but Target Plus sellers ship their own orders. Brands should choose their Target model with that gap in mind.

title: Walmart’s seller scorecard decides who wins the marketplace
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Walmart’s seller scorecard looks like a compliance check. It is really how Walmart picks its best sellers, and brands should manage it as a growth plan.

title: Five e-commerce business models now compete for the same shopper
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Retail, marketplaces, DTC, curated platforms and social commerce now compete for one shopper. Brands should give each model a distinct job, not pick one.

title: Ecommerce unit economics: profitable on paper, short of cash
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: A product can earn a healthy margin per unit and still drain cash. With freight and lead times stretched in 2021, model when cash moves, not just margin.

title: Mercado Pago and Mercado Ads belong in every Mercado Libre plan
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: On Mercado Libre, payments and advertising shape whether a sale happens. Brands should plan for Mercado Pago and Mercado Ads, not just the listing.

title: Amazon traffic means nothing without conversion
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: With Amazon clicks at $1.20, each point of conversion is worth more than extra traffic. Fix the listing before buying visits that cost more than they earn.

title: Zalando Marketing Services: buy the data to answer a question
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Zalando sells consumer insights and marketing through Zalando Marketing Services. Brands should buy it to answer specific questions, not as a general add-on.

title: Walmart’s private brands decide where marketplace sellers can win
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Walmart’s private brands hold the low-price end of many categories. Marketplace sellers win by offering what Walmart’s own range does not, not by undercutting.

title: Retail media needs both the spreadsheet and the strategist
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Automation now handles much of Amazon’s bidding, but it optimizes toward goals someone else sets. Retail media needs analysts and strategists working as one.

title: Amazon opens registration for Accelerate 2021, its virtual seller conference on October 20 and 21
author: Kwontified
desc: On September 8, 2021, Amazon opened registration for Accelerate 2021, a free virtual conference for its third-party sellers to be held on October 20 and…

title: Diversifying beyond Amazon with Instagram: own the customer
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Brands diversifying beyond Amazon often judge Instagram on its sales. Its value as a hedge is the customer relationship and demand it builds outside Amazon.

title: Pet on Amazon 2021: the second order matters more than the first
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Pet spending passed $100 billion in 2020 and more of it moved online. On Amazon, the value of a pet brand lies in the repeat order, so plan for the second sale.

title: Run Amazon on seven performance dimensions, not just the ads
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Most Amazon reviews focus on ads because that data is easiest to see. Seven dimensions, from traffic to account health, show where results are won or lost.

title: Shopping inside TikTok: what the Shopify test means for brands
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: TikTok’s Shopify pilot adds a shopping tab and product links. It suits brands whose products already spread on TikTok and who can make content to match.

title: TikTok tests in-app shopping with Shopify merchants
author: Kwontified
desc: On August 24, 2021, TikTok and Shopify announced an expanded partnership that lets Shopify merchants add a shopping tab to their TikTok profiles, Shopify…

title: Three retail media metrics that show which strategy is winning
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: The highest ROAS rarely marks the best retail media strategy. Marginal return, profit after ads and share of category search show which approach is winning.

title: Zalando private label: kept small so brands trust the platform
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Zalando narrowed its own labels to essentials in 2019 and is growing its Partner Program fast. Brands can treat it as a platform, while watching basics.

title: Amazon’s fee structure punishes low prices, so redesign the offer
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon’s fees are largely charged per unit and per click, so they eat low-priced products first. Brands should redesign packs, prices and ranges around them.

title: A Target Plus P&L: strong unit margins, heavy fixed costs
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: A Target Plus sale can carry a healthy unit margin, but low volume means fixed costs decide profitability. Build the P&L order by order, then add the overhead.

title: Q4 2021 budget phasing: the holiday is a season, not a weekend
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Cyber Week’s share of holiday online spending fell in 2020 as the season spread out. Phase Q4 2021 budgets from October onward, not around a single weekend.

title: Retail media metrics beyond ROAS: four signs of health
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: ROAS is falling across Amazon as costs rise, but it cannot say whether a program is healthy. Four measures give leaders a fuller view of what spend builds.

title: Amazon’s Q2 2021 results: slower sales make clicks more expensive
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon’s online store sales grew 13% in Q2 2021 while advertising grew 87%. Slower shopper growth with more advertisers means costlier clicks into the holiday.

title: Walmart marketplace sellers depend on grocery shoppers
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Walmart’s grocery trips bring the traffic its marketplace sellers sell to. Sellers should pick products that fit that trip and advertise where shoppers search.

title: Q2 2021 Amazon Sponsored Ads benchmark: Prime Day bought volume
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Q2 2021 Amazon ad results combine Prime Day in June with ten weeks of rising CPCs. Split the quarter to see what Prime Day bought and what it cost.

title: Back-to-school 2021 starts earlier, so plans must too
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Shoppers plan to spend most of their 2021 back-to-school budgets by the end of July. Brands need stock and advertising in place weeks earlier than usual.

title: Rising Amazon CPCs: how much is the market and how much is you
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon CPCs rose about a third in a year. Before blaming the market, split your own increase into auction inflation, keyword mix and your bids.

title: Grocery on Amazon in 2021 is a habit business with a new rival
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Online grocery cooled in 2021 while Amazon opened Fresh stores and launched Aplenty. Grocery brands should win the repeat order and watch Amazon’s own label.

title: FBA storage limits reward the brands that send less stock now
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon now limits FBA stock by storage type and IPI score. To fit more holiday inventory in Q4, brands should clear slow stock and ship smaller amounts now.

title: Port congestion will decide who has stock for the 2021 holiday
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Record imports and container rates up 346% in a year mean some shelves will run short this holiday. On Amazon, sales flow to whoever is in stock.

title: Amazon is the third force in digital advertising, at the shelf
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon now takes about a tenth of US digital ad spending, behind Google and Facebook. Its strength is the shelf, so brands must balance it against reach.

title: Andy Jassy becomes Amazon’s chief executive as Jeff Bezos moves to executive chair
author: Kwontified
desc: On July 5, 2021, Andy Jassy officially became chief executive of Amazon, taking over from founder Jeff Bezos, who now holds the title of executive…

title: Prime Day 2021 lessons: everyone now competes for traffic
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: At Prime Day 2021, rival retailers, Amazon and brands all chased the traffic Amazon created while discounts stayed modest. Plan the next event for traffic.

title: Prime Day 2021 results landed in the lower half of the range
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Prime Day 2021 grew about 7% on 2020, with smaller orders and faster marketplace growth, which puts it in the lower half of a sensible pre-event range.

title: Google delays the end of third-party cookies in Chrome to late 2023
author: Kwontified
desc: On June 24, 2021, Google said it would delay its plan to phase out third-party cookies in its Chrome browser, which advertisers use to track people across…

title: Health and household on Amazon moved from scarcity to scrutiny
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: In 2020, health and household on Amazon was a race for stock. In 2021 it is a test of documentation and trust, and brands that prove quality keep shoppers.

title: Early read: Prime Day 2021 set a record for third-party sellers, with no total disclosed
author: Kwontified
desc: On June 23, 2021, Amazon said Prime Day 2021, held June 21 and 22, was the biggest two-day period ever for its third-party sellers, whose sales grew…

title: Zalando’s fashion ecosystem rewards brands that buy in stages
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Zalando now offers selling, fulfillment, marketing and store connections. Each is convenient; together they concentrate risk. Buy them one at a time.

title: Target Plus lends brands a halo that Amazon’s open shelf cannot
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Target Plus has fewer than 300 sellers against Amazon’s millions. Its scarcity lends brands a halo of Target’s curation, which matters more than its volume.

title: Instagram checkout fees make it a sales channel to price like one
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Facebook’s waiver of Instagram checkout fees runs through June 2021. Once a 5% fee applies, Instagram should be priced like a marketplace, order by order.

title: A fractured org chart holds back the Amazon business
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Amazon turns a brand’s ads, stock, price and content into one result. Brands that split those decisions across four teams lose value at every handoff.

title: Mercado Libre or Amazon in Latin America depends on the country
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Mercado Libre earns most of its revenue in Brazil and Argentina, while Amazon leads in Mexico. Brands entering Latin America should choose by country.

title: How to change agencies without losing Amazon momentum or budget
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Amazon keeps only 90 days of campaign change history. Brands changing agencies should own the accounts, plan the handover and avoid switching before Prime Day.

title: Amazon announces Prime Day 2021 for June 21 and 22
author: Kwontified
desc: On June 2, 2021, Amazon said Prime Day 2021 will run on June 21 and 22, with more than 2 million deals, according to its press release .

title: A Prime Day 2021 forecast needs a range, not 2020’s number
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Prime Day 2020 ran in October and 2019 in July, so June has no clean comparison. Forecast 2021 as a range built from both years, not last year plus growth.

title: The future of shopping is a tech fight run on brands’ data
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Google, Facebook and TikTok now compete with Amazon for where shopping starts. Every one needs brands’ product data, so a clean feed is now core infrastructure.

title: Amazon bid automation can starve your most profitable products
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon’s bid automation favors products with the most conversion history, which can starve newer, higher-margin ones. Structure campaigns so it cannot.

title: Amazon’s review crackdown shows who owns a brand’s reputation
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Amazon’s removal of Aukey and Mpow shows reviews are among a brand’s most valuable assets, and that Amazon decides if they count. Earn them, never buy them.

title: Amazon’s algorithms are the store manager brands never meet
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: On Amazon, models decide which offer wins, where products rank and what ads cost. Brands cannot persuade that store manager, only change what it sees.

title: Prime Day in June squeezes the 2021 planning year for brands
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Amazon moved Prime Day from October 2020 to June 2021, leaving eight months between events and only weeks to prepare. Brands must plan the year around it.

title: Amazon removes Aukey and Mpow listings after a fake-review leak
author: Kwontified
desc: Most products from Aukey and Mpow, two popular brands of phone chargers, headphones and other electronics accessories, disappeared from Amazon around May…

title: Amazon ad growth in Q1 shows more sellers bidding per shopper
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon’s ad revenue grew 77% in Q1 2021, far faster than its 44% sales growth. The gap is more sellers bidding for each shopper, and Prime Day will widen it.

title: Chinese sellers on Amazon: when your factory becomes your rival
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Three quarters of new Amazon sellers in January 2021 were based in China, many selling factory direct. Brands should compete on what a factory cannot copy.

title: Apple’s change makes the retail media closed loop worth more
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Apple’s tracking prompt weakens social ad measurement but not retail media, which sees the sale itself. Budgets will move toward it, and prices with them.

title: Amazon’s first-quarter sales rise 44% as it moves Prime Day into the second quarter
author: Kwontified
desc: On April 29, 2021, Amazon reported net sales of $108.5 billion for the first quarter, up 44% from a year earlier, and said it would hold Prime Day during…

title: Legacy brands on marketplaces need a new operating model
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Legacy brands were built to sell to retail buyers. Marketplaces reward whoever controls listing, price and stock daily, which calls for a new operating model.

title: Q1 2021 Amazon Sponsored Ads benchmark: split out the stimulus
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Q1 2021 Amazon ad results mix a quiet January with a March lifted by $1,400 stimulus payments. Split the quarter before you compare CPC, conversion or ROAS.

title: Apple’s App Tracking Transparency goes live with iOS 14.5
author: Kwontified
desc: On April 26, 2021, Apple released iOS 14.5, which requires apps to ask iPhone and iPad users for permission before tracking their activity across other…

title: Retail media redefines brand building as new customers counted
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Retail media measures brand building in new-to-brand orders, which makes it accountable but can miss the memory brands build before shoppers buy.

title: Amazon Best Seller rank rewards the brands already winning
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon’s Best Sellers rank updates hourly from recent and past sales, so sales buy visibility that buys more sales. Fund momentum where it compounds.

title: Mother’s Day 2021 rewards brands shoppers can find by recipient
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Mother’s Day spending hit a record $26.7 billion in 2020, and a third of shoppers look first for gift suggestions. Brands win by being findable by recipient.

title: Walmart competes with Amazon for the weekly trip, not the website
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon’s online lead looks decisive by size. Walmart competes on frequency instead, the weekly grocery trip tied to a $98 membership, so plan for both.

title: Handbags on Amazon need trust, so Amazon is fighting fakes
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Amazon is suing counterfeiters alongside luxury houses because authenticity decides whether handbags sell there. Brands should use the tools and own the job.

title: Zalando size and fit advice turns returns into an advantage
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: A third of Zalando’s returns come down to size. Its size advice learns from return data no single brand can match, so brands should feed it and learn from it.

title: Footwear on Amazon after Nike: the shoes stayed behind
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Nike stopped selling to Amazon in 2019, yet its shoes stayed on Amazon through resellers. Footwear leaders should ask whether they can afford the same choice.

title: Live shopping in China works because buying stays in the stream
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Taobao Live sold more than RMB400 billion of goods in 2020. The lesson for Instagram live shopping is the purchase path, not the hosts or the hype.

title: DTC brands are turning to Amazon as paid social costs rise
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Many DTC brands were founded on selling only through their own sites. Rising paid social costs pushed them onto Amazon, which needs planning as a real channel.

title: Zalando’s selectiveness is what brands are paying for
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Zalando reached 38.7 million active customers in 2020 while choosing who sells and how. That selectiveness is what brands pay for and must keep earning.

title: Instagram checkout moves the customer from the brand to the app
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: In-app checkout shortens the path to purchase, but Instagram sends the order emails and keeps the contact, so brands should decide what they are handing over.

title: Walmart Marketplace grows only as fast as its deliveries
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Walmart Marketplace more than doubled its sellers in 2020, yet only 430 of them used Walmart’s own fulfillment. Delivery speed decides who captures the growth.

title: Apparel on Amazon got easier when Amazon gave brands control
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Clothing store sales fell 26.4% in 2020, and Amazon’s Luxury Stores handed brands control of price and selection. The apparel case against Amazon needs a rerun.

title: Walmart Connect earns Walmart more per dollar than its shelves
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Walmart earns about five cents of operating profit per dollar of US sales and far more per ad dollar, which is why Walmart Connect will shape supplier talks.

title: Amazon Marketing Cloud brings the brand’s data into Amazon’s room
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Brands have long asked Amazon to send them more ad data. Amazon Marketing Cloud answers the other way: bring your data into a room that Amazon controls.

title: Amazon DSP pays off when search ads run out of shoppers
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Sponsored ads only reach shoppers who are already searching, so Amazon DSP earns budget once the next search dollar returns less than a tested DSP dollar.

title: Vendor Central is Amazon’s choice now, not the brand’s
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: In March 2019, tens of thousands of Amazon vendors found no weekly purchase order waiting, which is why Vendor Central now deserves a yearly review.

title: Instagram shopping will look weaker in reports than in sales
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Facebook expects Apple’s iOS 14 changes to weaken ad measurement from late Q1 2021, so Instagram shopping results may drop in reports before sales do.

title: Roundel is built like a media partner, so buy it like one
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Target built Roundel as an in-house media company that designs campaigns with brands, so planning it like a self-serve auction misses what it is.

title: Mercado Libre for brands is a local-currency business first
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Mercado Libre’s sales volume grew 117.1% in local terms and 62.1% in dollars in one quarter, so brands judging the channel in dollars are misreading it.

title: Target Plus sits outside the engine of Target’s growth
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Target’s holiday digital growth ran through store pickup and same-day delivery, and Target Plus items, shipped from sellers’ own warehouses, ride neither.

title: Amazon advertising revenue outran its sales in Q4 2020
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon’s ad-heavy revenue line grew 66% in Q4 2020 while units grew only 47%, so brands paid more advertising for every sale, and ROAS hid it.

title: Walmart Connect asks brands to merge budgets that sit apart
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Walmart Connect now sells ads on its site, in its stores and across the web, yet most brands split those budgets across three teams that rarely meet.

title: Jeff Bezos to hand Amazon’s CEO role to Andy Jassy in the third quarter
author: Kwontified
desc: On February 2, 2021, Amazon said founder Jeff Bezos will become executive chair in the third quarter of 2021 and Andy Jassy, who leads Amazon Web…

title: Walmart Marketplace sets your price floor everywhere you sell
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Walmart Marketplace pulls a listing when the same product is cheaper anywhere else, so one weekend sale on your own site can cost you the Walmart shelf.

title: Walmart renames its ad business Walmart Connect and plans a DSP with The Trade Desk
author: Kwontified
desc: On January 28, 2021, Walmart renamed its media business, previously Walmart Media Group, as Walmart Connect and set out plans to become one of the top ten…

title: NRF 2021 put product availability at the center of brand loyalty
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: At NRF 2021, retailers described anxious shoppers who switched brands when shelves went empty, which puts availability squarely on the brand team’s agenda.

title: An Amazon Sponsored Ads benchmark for Q4 2020 splits Prime Day
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Prime Day landed in October 2020, so any Q4 Amazon ad benchmark blends two auction peaks. Split the quarter before you judge your CPC or ROAS.

title: The Zalando Partner Program needs a new owner inside brands
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Most brands still meet Zalando twice a year at a buying appointment, while Zalando’s growth now comes from partners who list, price and stock their own range.

title: A Target Plus invitation goes to brands that fill a gap
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Brands that sell well on Amazon assume a Target Plus invitation rewards size, but Target’s own words say it rewards filling a hole in its assortment.

title: Mercado Libre’s growth asks brands to rethink Latin America
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Mercado Libre now ships and takes payment at a scale few distributors match, which turns Latin America into a question of who owns the customer.

title: Amazon’s delayed 2021 fee increase still needs a model now
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon pushed its 2021 FBA fee increase to June 1, and whatever it adds per unit will come straight off the ACoS each of your products can afford.

title: Brands undervalue Instagram shopping by measuring it as marketing
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Instagram gave shopping a tab on its home screen in November 2020, yet most brands still grade the account on likes, two desks from the sales target.

title: CPG brands move budgets to retail media networks they can measure
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Retail media dashboards report a sale by Monday, so CPG trade money is moving there, but the sale they report is not always one the ads caused.

title: Marketplace inventory in 2020 sat behind a gate brands don’t hold
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: In 2020 brands learned that stock in their own warehouse is not stock on the marketplace shelf. The link between them now runs on someone else’s rules.

title: The marketplace ad tax rises with every seller a retailer adds
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Advertising has become a fee that marketplace sellers pay on top of commission, and it grows with the number of sellers competing for a fixed set of placements.

title: E-commerce taught traditional brands every order pays its own way
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: In the store, a cheap item rides home in a full cart. Online it needs its own box, and 2020 showed traditional brands which products could carry that cost.

title: Subscribe and Save in a demand surge pays back after it ends
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: When every unit sells anyway, the Subscribe and Save discount looks like wasted margin. It is the price of the customers still ordering after the surge.

title: Marketplaces in 2020 became the default retail model worldwide
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: In 2020 Amazon, Walmart, Zalando, Mercado Libre and even Google and Facebook grew by letting others sell. Brands still decide marketplace by marketplace.

title: 2021 Amazon ROAS targets built on 2020 will cut the wrong ads
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: ROAS is a ratio of conversion rate to click price, and 2020 moved both for reasons that had nothing to do with your ads. Plan 2021 bids from click value.

title: Cyber Week 2020 exposed holiday budgets still built for five days
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: The 2020 holiday ran from Prime Day in October to Christmas, but most brands’ deal funding, stock and approvals were still organized around one weekend.

title: Cyber Week 2020 grew 21%, and the rest of November grew faster
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Cyber Week 2020 landed at the bottom of the forecasts while November as a whole grew about 31%. The gap is demand that moved, which changes how to grade it.

title: Price gouging on Amazon put brand names on prices they never set
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: In 2020’s price-gouging scare, shoppers read the brand on the bottle before the seller in small type, so brands carried the trust cost of prices set by others.

title: Early read: Cyber Week 2020 sets online records on Thanksgiving and Black Friday, below Adobe’s October forecast (preliminary)
author: Kwontified
desc: US shoppers spent a record $9 billion online on Black Friday, November 27, up 21.6% on 2019, and $5.1 billion on Thanksgiving Day, according to Adobe…

title: Amazon search ranking after a stockout is won back from a rival
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: A stockout does not just pause your Amazon search rank. It hands your sales history to the product that sold in your place, and that is what you must outsell.

title: Marketplace data shows demand weeks before purchase orders do
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Wholesale orders show what buyers decided. The marketplace team sees what shoppers did, often weeks earlier. In 2020 that gap decided who had stock.

title: Q4 deal planning: the second peak needs a shallower discount
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Prime Day in October and Black Friday in November sell to the same shoppers. The second deal buys fewer extra units, so on most products it should be shallower.

title: Walmart Marketplace growth puts more sellers on your item pages
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Walmart says its marketplace is the fastest-growing part of its online business. For brands, that means more sellers offering their products on Walmart.com.

title: A demand forecasting baseline for 2021 should skip 2020
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: A year-over-year forecast for 2021 will copy 2020’s panic weeks and moved events into next year. Take the shape from 2019 and the level from recent weeks.

title: Amazon sets Black Friday Deals Week for November 20 to 27, weeks after Walmart and Target opened theirs
author: Kwontified
desc: Amazon will run its US Black Friday Deals Week from Friday, November 20 through Black Friday, November 27, releasing tens of thousands of deals with new…

title: Instagram Shop is the window display that lockdown took away
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Lockdown closed the shop windows where shoppers found things they were not looking for. Instagram Shop now does that job, and few brands staff it.

title: Retail media kept its budget in 2020 because it shows the sale
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Retail media grew through 2020 while other ad budgets shrank, because it could show the sale next to the ad. That proof has a blind spot worth seeing.

title: Amazon ad growth in Q3 2020 says cheap clicks are over
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon’s ad line grew 51% in a quarter without Prime Day, and the growth came back through click prices. Spring bids are now losing auctions they used to win.

title: October Prime Day rewarded brands that could decide in two weeks
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Amazon gave 15 days’ notice and rivals answered within a day. The holiday calendar now moves by announcement, and slow approval chains lose.

title: Prime Day 2020 beat its forecast by 5%; December will grade it
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Estimates put Prime Day 2020 about 5% above eMarketer’s forecast. How much was pulled from November will not be known until the holidays are over.

title: Shoppers forgave 2020’s late deliveries, but only on loan
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Shoppers forgave late deliveries in 2020 when they were warned before paying. Most say that patience is temporary, and holiday deadlines will test it.

title: Early read: Prime Day 2020 ends with panel data only and Amazon’s tally still to come (preliminary)
author: Kwontified
desc: Amazon’s first October Prime Day ended at midnight Pacific time on October 14, 2020, after 48 hours of deals in 19 countries.

title: Cyber Week 2020 is now a November season, and the plan is due now
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Walmart and Target have spread Black Friday across November. After an October Prime Day, the deal, stock and budget calls for Cyber Week are due this week.

title: Contribution margin by ASIN, not one ACoS target, sets ad budgets
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: A single ACoS target averages thin-margin and thick-margin products together. Price each ASIN’s ads from its own contribution margin instead.

title: Holiday gifting in 2020 makes the shipping box the gift wrap
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: When the gift travels without the giver, the product page, the delivery date and the box do the work the giver used to do. Brands should plan for it.

title: An Amazon incrementality holdout test needs weeks, not days
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Daily Amazon sales swing more than ads move them, so a one-week holdout proves nothing. Size the test to the noise before you switch anything off.

title: Amazon’s second AdCon ran online and steered brands toward streaming TV and video ads
author: Kwontified
desc: Amazon Advertising opened AdCon 2020, its second annual conference for advertisers, online on September 30, 2020, and used it to push brands beyond search…

title: Holiday 2020 shipping capacity, not Black Friday, sets the plan
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Carriers priced holiday 2020 against February volumes. Brands that plan back from the last promised delivery, not forward from Black Friday, keep margin.

title: Amazon repeat purchase data lets sellers price a new customer
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon Accelerate gave sellers repeat-purchase data. Its real use is setting how much a new customer is worth, and so how high to bid going into Prime Day.

title: Amazon sets Prime Day 2020 for October 13-14, with a $10 credit for buying from small businesses first
author: Kwontified
desc: Amazon will hold Prime Day 2020 on October 13 and 14, starting at midnight Pacific time on the Tuesday, the company announced on September 28, 2020, CBS…

title: Work-from-home products now sell to the employee, not the office
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Monitors, webcams and office chairs used to be bought by a purchasing desk. In 2020 the buyer became the employee at home, and the shelf changed with her.

title: Walmart+ leaves marketplace sellers outside its membership perks
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Walmart+ is built around the store: a fuel pump, a checkout lane and a store-picked basket. Marketplace sellers get the traffic but none of the member perks.

title: Retail media budget cuts should start with your best-ROAS ads
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: When a retail media budget has to shrink, cutting the lowest-ROAS ads first removes the spend creating sales and keeps the spend that was only counting them.

title: Beauty on Amazon in 2020 rewarded products that need no tester
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: When beauty counters closed and testers became display-only, the products that held up online were the ones a shopper could choose without trying them first.

title: Instagram checkout fees cost less than 5% against your own site
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Facebook’s 5% checkout fee already covers payment processing, so against your own site it costs about half a dollar an order. Conversion decides the rest.

title: Amazon Accelerate 2020: Brand Follow, repeat-purchase data and $100 million to promote small sellers
author: Kwontified
desc: Amazon opened Amazon Accelerate, a new virtual conference for US sellers, on September 1, 2020 with two tools for brand owners and a promise to spend an…

title: Prime Day 2020 planning can’t wait for Amazon to name a date
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Amazon has moved Prime Day 2020 into the fourth quarter without naming a date. Brands that wait for it will make three planning decisions too late.

title: Walmart launches Walmart+ on September 15: free same-day delivery from stores for $98 a year
author: Kwontified
desc: Walmart announced Walmart+ on September 1, 2020, a membership that will cost $98 a year or $12.95 a month and opens to all US customers on September 15…

title: Mercado Libre logistics now sort sellers by who carries the box
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: When Correios workers struck in August, Mercado Livre told shoppers to buy listings marked as delivering normally. The carrier now decides who gets the sale.

title: Blanket Amazon ad spend cuts in March gave rivals cheaper clicks
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: In March many brands switched off Amazon ads by budget line. Advertisers that stayed bought clicks for far less, and the cut was made far from the shelf.

title: Zalando Partner Program growth moves stock risk onto brands
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Zalando’s GMV keeps outgrowing its revenue because partners, not Zalando, own more of the stock. More listings put more markdown risk on brands.

title: Latin America’s e-commerce leap will last where buying is routine
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Mercado Libre sold twice as many items this spring. The habits that last will be the repeat basket and the digital wallet, not the one-off splurge.

title: Q4 2020 ad budgets should follow the last dollar, not 2019
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Q4 2020 has more peaks than 2019, and one has no date yet. Fund each day until its last dollar earns your target return, and keep a reserve.

title: Zalando partners recovered first where brands controlled stock
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Zalando’s partner sales doubled in the spring of 2020. The brands that recovered first already controlled what Zalando’s shoppers saw, and when.

title: Target’s same-day boom passed Target Plus partners by
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Target’s online surge ran through its stores, and Target Plus items ship from partners’ warehouses. The curated marketplace kept trust and missed the trunk.

title: Amazon Q2 2020 other revenue rose 41% while click prices fell 41%
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon’s ad-heavy other revenue grew 41% in Q2 2020 while a typical Sponsored Products advertiser spent 22% more. The gap is new bidders, and Q4 prices them in.

title: Live shopping sells what a host can touch, test and vouch for
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: China’s live shopping boom sells what a trusted host can handle on camera at an impulse price. Western platforms now have the tools; most brands lack the host.

title: Footwear on Amazon now has to answer the fitting-room question
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: With shoe stores shut for weeks, footwear on Amazon must do the fitting the store once did. Brands that answer size and fit on the page keep the sale.

title: Instagram opens a Shop in Explore, with in-app checkout through Facebook Pay
author: Kwontified
desc: Instagram began rolling out a redesigned Instagram Shop in the US on July 16, 2020, a shopping destination inside the app’s Explore section where people…

title: Back-to-school 2020 will be late, online and bought with no list
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Most families planning back-to-school 2020 still lack a supply list and plan to shop online. Brands should expect a late, long season decided on search pages.

title: Walmart Fulfillment Services turns two-day into a stock decision
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Walmart Fulfillment Services prices the two-day promise per unit, not per mile. The catch is stock that must wait in Walmart’s building before anyone orders.

title: When wholesale orders stop, the brand owns the inventory risk
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: A department store that stops ordering is not sulking; it is full. The stock it did not buy is now the brand’s to place, and marketplaces are where it will go.

title: Walmart Marketplace approval screens the seller, then the product
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Walmart’s Shopify deal opens an app, not the gate. Approval still turns on whether Walmart expects you to ship like Walmart and sell what it lacks.

title: Amazon customer service starts with the delivery date you promise
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: When Amazon deliveries slip, the shopper’s complaint goes wherever Amazon routes it, rarely to the brand’s service desk. The date you promise is your service.

title: Walmart Sponsored Products bid floors decide which items go first
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Walmart’s $0.30 manual bid floor and first-price auction set a minimum conversion rate for each item. Start with the items that clear it, not the cheapest.

title: Trusted brands gained when the aisle shrank to best-known items
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: When shelves emptied, makers and retailers cut to their core items. Trusted brands and store labels gained, and the long tail between them lost its place.

title: Off-Amazon audiences in DSP are scored only at Amazon’s checkout
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon DSP’s off-Amazon ads are credited only with Amazon purchases, which undercounts sales elsewhere and overcounts buyers who were coming anyway.

title: Home and kitchen on Amazon favored brands that ship themselves
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Demand for bread makers and cookware surged just as Amazon stopped restocking home goods, so the spring’s winners were the sellers who held their own stock.

title: Shopify sellers will bring their discounts to the Walmart Buy Box
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Walmart’s price parity rule caps a seller’s Walmart price at its lowest price elsewhere, so new Shopify sellers bring their own-store discounts to the Buy Box.

title: Walmart opens its marketplace to Shopify merchants and expects 1,200 to join this year
author: Kwontified
desc: Walmart and Shopify said on June 15, 2020 that US merchants on Shopify can now apply to sell on Walmart.com through a new sales channel inside Shopify…

title: Pandemic demand worth planning around kept growing in May
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Stockpiling faded by late May while online grocery kept adding households. The shifts that grew after the panic are the ones a brand’s plan should keep.

title: The Amazon DSP minimum turns a retargeting test into prospecting
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: A mid-size brand’s retargeting pool cannot absorb the Amazon DSP minimum, so most of that money buys strangers. Plan and judge it as prospecting from day one.

title: Curbside pickup hands the local order to the store shelf
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Curbside pickup orders are picked from the store’s own shelf, so the brands that win them are the ones the store buyer chose at the line review.

title: Stopped Amazon vendor purchase orders empty the shelf weeks later
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: A paused Amazon purchase order does no damage on the day it stops. The cost arrives weeks later, when Amazon’s stock runs out and someone else takes the page.

title: Store closures put a brand’s clearance in someone else’s hands
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: When a department store liquidates, the brand’s stock is no longer the brand’s. Without a marketplace plan, others decide where and at what price it sells.

title: Amazon price gouging rules compare you with your recent prices
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon’s fair pricing rule measures a price against recent prices on and off Amazon, so ending a discount can look like a spike. Move prices in steps.

title: Facebook Shops gives the social team a store to run
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Facebook Shops puts a full store on a brand’s Instagram profile, the account its social team runs. The work of a store belongs to people who rarely touch it.

title: Walmart will discontinue Jet.com as US e-commerce sales rise 74%
author: Kwontified
desc: Walmart said on May 19, 2020 that it will discontinue Jet.com, the online retailer it bought in 2016 for $3.3 billion, as it reported a 74% rise in US…

title: Facebook launches Shops, one free storefront across Facebook and Instagram
author: Kwontified
desc: Facebook launched Facebook Shops on May 19, 2020, letting a business set up one online store that shoppers can reach from its Facebook Page and its…

title: Multi-channel fulfillment cuts safety stock by pooling demand
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon MCF is usually judged on its per-order fee. Its bigger effect is pooling: one stock for two channels needs less safety stock than two stocks do.

title: First-time online grocery shoppers meet your brand as a thumbnail
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Millions of households ordered groceries online for the first time this spring. They found brands in a search box, not an aisle the brand paid to shape.

title: With FBA restock limits lifted, IPI decides next quarter’s space
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon lifted its FBA quantity limits on May 9. Sending every slow seller now lowers IPI and can shrink next quarter’s storage space for everything.

title: Panic brand switching sticks where shoppers reorder by habit
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Two-thirds of US shoppers tried a new brand this spring, mostly because theirs was gone. The ones they keep are the ones their order history now remembers.

title: Amazon Q1 2020 other revenue grew 44% and barely saw March
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon’s ad line grew 44% in Q1 2020, but one bad week moves a quarterly rate by a thirteenth. Read April in your own CPC and conversion data instead.

title: Zalando fit and returns decide the sale long after the order
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: On Zalando about half of what sells comes back, so a sale counts only when the shopper keeps the size. Brands arriving this spring must plan for fit first.

title: The Q1 2020 Amazon ad benchmark averages two different markets
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Public Q1 2020 Amazon ad benchmarks show Sponsored Products spend up 24% and CPCs up 9%, but the quarter mixes a normal market and a disrupted one.

title: The Walmart online shopper now starts with a grocery list
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Over the past year the Walmart online shopper became, above all, a grocery shopper. In April 2020 that path runs through pickup and the grocery app.

title: Amazon Vine buys a new product an honest verdict, not a good one
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon Vine lets brands seed early reviews within the rules, but Amazon picks the reviewers and the stars. Enroll only products ready to be judged.

title: Grocery on Amazon in 2020 has more shoppers than delivery slots
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Online grocery use more than doubled in March 2020, but Amazon closed Pantry and waitlisted new Fresh customers. The new habit is forming at other stores.

title: Amazon will let more non-essential products into FBA this week, in capped quantities
author: Kwontified
desc: Amazon said on April 13, 2020 that it will let more products into its fulfillment centers later this week, easing the March limit that kept most…

title: Amazon Live is free, but its free viewers are your own shoppers
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: An Amazon Live stream costs nothing to broadcast, but the free placement mostly shows it to shoppers already on your product page. Count the new viewers.

title: Mother’s Day 2020 gifts must travel, and marketplaces sort them
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: With brunch cancelled and families apart, Mother’s Day 2020 gifts move to marketplaces, where warehouse rules decide what arrives by May 10.

title: Out-of-stock Amazon ads hand their keywords to the next product
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: When a best seller runs out on Amazon, its Sponsored Products keywords keep bidding for whatever is left in the ad group, at the best seller’s price.

title: Health and household on Amazon became a rationed aisle in March
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: In March 2020 Amazon began deciding which health and household products get warehouse space, at what price and how fast they arrive. Brands must plan for it.

title: Amazon Posts is worth what its clicks would cost you in ads
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon Posts is free, but its value is the ad spend its clicks replace, discounted for weaker intent. Price Posts against your CPC before you staff it.

title: Beauty brands on Amazon: holding out leaves resellers in charge
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Salon and prestige beauty brands that stay off Amazon still appear there, sold by resellers at cut prices. The authorized-seller question starts at home.

title: With FBA inbound capped, Amazon ads buy timing, not extra sales
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: When FBA cannot restock a product, its ads stop adding sales and only sell the same units sooner. Re-plan ad budgets around the stockout date.

title: Shoppers read Amazon product reviews to learn how a product fails
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Most shoppers check reviews, and most look for the bad ones first. They want to know how a product fails and whether that failure matters to them.

title: Amazon limits FBA inbound shipments to household staples, medical supplies and other high-demand products until April 5
author: Kwontified
desc: Amazon told sellers on March 17, 2020 that its US and European fulfillment centers are “temporarily prioritizing household staples, medical supplies and…

title: Brand Analytics market basket ranks the popular, not the paired
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon’s market basket report ranks what is often bought with your product, which favors popular items. Check the base rate before you bundle.

title: Apparel on Amazon in 2020: brands can leave, products stay
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Nike’s exit showed apparel brands can stop selling to Amazon but cannot take their products off it. The 2020 choice is who stands behind the listing.

title: Falling Amazon CPCs are a bargain only if conversion held
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: A cheaper click is good news only if it still converts. When Amazon CPCs fall, reset each bid from what the click is worth, not from what it now costs.

title: Walmart Media Group opened its search shelf before its store data
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Walmart Media Group now sells walmart.com search ads self-serve, but its store data is still locked away. Brands should decide who owns that shelf now.

title: Amazon DSP in 2020 is worth its shopping data, not its screens
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon now lets rival platforms sell some of its screens but keeps its shopping data inside Amazon DSP. Price every DSP line on the audience, not the placement.

title: Vendor Central in 2020 negotiates for the slower half of Amazon
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Amazon’s own store grew 15% last quarter while seller services grew 30%. Vendor negotiations should start from where a brand’s Amazon units are really sold.

title: Instagram shopping ads should be judged per order, not per click
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Instagram shopping ads put a product page between the ad and your site, so site clicks look dear while orders can be cheaper. Compare them on cost per order.

title: Roundel sells what Target knows about its shoppers, not its shelf
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Target built Roundel from its marketing team to sell what it knows about identified shoppers, in stores and online. Plan it as media, not trade spend.

title: Mercado Libre fees in Brazil turn on a single R$120 line
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: On Mercado Livre, orders under R$120 pay a R$5 fee per unit and pricier new items must ship free. Brands should price packs around that line, not across it.

title: Target Plus shoppers assume Target picked your product
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Target.com puts Target Plus items on the same shelf as Target’s own, under the same promises, so partners should build every listing like a Target buy.

title: Zalando Partner Program pays best on items Zalando would buy
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: On Zalando, the Partner Program earns a brand most on its surest sellers, the same items Zalando’s buyers most want to own. Split your range by sell-through.

title: Walmart Marketplace in 2020 sits outside your store buyer’s aisle
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Walmart runs store and online merchandising as separate teams, and its marketplace answers to the online side. Brands need a plan for each counterpart.

title: Amazon Q4 2019 other revenue outgrew units sold nearly two to one
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon’s ad-heavy other revenue grew 41% in Q4 2019 while paid units grew 22%, so the ad money behind each unit sold rose about 16% in a year.

title: Amazon Stores serve shoppers who have already chosen the brand
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Most visitors to an Amazon Store have already picked the brand and want help choosing within it. Stores built like a lookbook leave them to fend for themselves.

title: Target Plus extends the aisles where Target’s stores struggle
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Target’s invitation-only marketplace grew slowly in 2019 and sits in the categories its stores sold weakest this holiday. The invitation is a merchant’s tool.

title: Amazon 2020 fee changes favor pricier items over cheap ones
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon’s February 18 fees cut percentage charges on pricier items and raise fixed charges on every unit. Model them by price before they hit margin.

title: NRF 2020 showed store staff now working for the online order
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: At NRF 2020 Walmart and Sam’s Club described moving their people to the floor and the pickup counter. For brands, the aisle display now reaches fewer buyers.

title: Valentine’s Day gifts on Amazon now reach far beyond the partner
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Almost two-fifths of a Valentine’s budget now goes to family, friends, classmates and pets. That shopping starts in January and runs on different listings.

title: Sponsored Display views audiences pay off on slow purchases
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Sponsored Display views targets anyone who looked in the past 30 days. That window fits a stroller’s purchase cycle and wastes money on a phone case.

title: The 2010s moved the start of shopping to Amazon product search
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Over the 2010s shoppers moved the first step of buying into Amazon product search. Most brands are still organized around the store they left.

title: Total ACoS shows if Amazon ads grew sales or just claimed them
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: ACoS divides ad spend by the sales Amazon credits to ads, so it can improve while total sales stand still. Total ACoS, and its change, shows what the ads added.

title: Walmart’s online shopper wants a basket; Amazon’s wants an item
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Walmart.com’s shoppers look like Amazon’s on a survey, but they arrive for a different job: a household basket built around a store trip, not a single search.

title: Amazon raises FBA fees about 3% and cuts some referral fees, effective February 18
author: Kwontified
desc: Amazon told US sellers on December 23, 2019 that its 2020 fee changes take effect on February 18, 2020: fulfillment fees rise by about 3%, select referral…

title: Keyword harvesting on Amazon needs more clicks than it gets
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Most keyword harvesting acts on a handful of clicks, where a search term’s conversion rate is mostly noise. Set click thresholds before you move or block terms.

title: Marketplaces in 2019 charged brands for the aisle and the truck
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: In 2019 marketplaces earned more from selling visibility and delivery speed than from the sale itself, and brands’ budgets have not caught up with that shift.

title: The 2020 plan should copy 2019’s events, not its dates
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Most 2020 plans start from 2019’s sales by date. The holidays move, so a plan built on dates books false growth in one month and false losses in the next.

title: Amazon bars sellers from using FedEx Ground for Prime orders through the holidays
author: Kwontified
desc: Amazon has barred third-party sellers from using FedEx Ground to deliver Prime orders through the holidays, saying FedEx’s delivery performance is…

title: Cyber Week 2019 belonged to retailers who own the calendar
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Cyber Week 2019 set records, but the lasting change is who ran it: retailers set the dates, the deals and the pickup counter, and brands planned around them.

title: A founder’s first Amazon listing is a self-portrait, not a shelf
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Founders write their first Amazon listing as a story about themselves. Shoppers read it as one option on a shared shelf, and the gap shows in sales.

title: Cyber Week 2019 early read: Thanksgiving and Black Friday set online records but land just under Adobe’s forecast
author: Kwontified
desc: Preliminary figures from Adobe Analytics show US shoppers spent a record $4.2 billion online on Thanksgiving Day and $7.4 billion on Black Friday 2019…

title: Amazon variation listings share one rating; merge only true twins
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: An Amazon variation family shares one review pool and one star rating. Merge children shoppers would swap; split any child that could earn a different score.

title: Zalando’s profits show Europe is many home markets, not one
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Zalando makes money in Germany, Austria and Switzerland and loses it elsewhere. Brands should plan European marketplaces as separate home markets.

title: Brand loyalty on Amazon lives in the 22% of searches naming you
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Most Amazon searches name a need rather than a brand, so loyalty shows up only when shoppers type your name. Brands must win the other searches too.

title: Amazon sets Black Friday Deals Week for November 22 to 29, with Cyber Monday deals on December 2
author: Kwontified
desc: Amazon will run its Black Friday Deals Week in the US from Friday, November 22 through Black Friday on November 29, with new deals “all day, every day,”…

title: Shoppers buy sustainability claims they can check on the page
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Sustainability-marketed products took half of US packaged-goods growth, but on a product page only the claims a shopper can verify carry weight.

title: Gift returns are decided by people who never chose the gift
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: After December the person deciding whether your product stays is the recipient, a customer you never marketed to. Plan January returns for that person.

title: Amazon AdCon 2019 was a recruiting drive for your auctions
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon’s first brand ad conference trained hundreds of new bidders. For brands already advertising, that means more rivals in every Q4 auction.

title: Wholesale to marketplace: a brand trades seasons for days
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: A brand moving from wholesale to marketplace selling swaps a seasonal clock for a daily one, and most of the change is in who may decide what, and how fast.

title: Amazon coupons vs price cuts: only one resets your deal baseline
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon’s ranking rewards units, not the discount that sold them, so choosing a coupon or a price cut turns on who gets the discount and on your deal price.

title: Marketplace channel conflict starts with what your buyers can see
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: When a brand lists on Amazon, its wholesale buyers read the move through the prices, products and priority they can see, and channel conflict follows.

title: Cyber Week 2019 crosses into December, and monthly plans break
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: A late Thanksgiving pushes Cyber Monday 2019 into December, so plans, budgets and targets built by calendar month will misread the season unless changed now.

title: Marketplace price parity now binds through retailers’ discounts
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon dropped its price parity clause, but retailer-funded discounts now set a brand’s lowest public price, and every marketplace price check follows it.

title: Vendor Central relationships fail where the buyer became a system
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Brands run Amazon vendor accounts like a buyer relationship while Amazon runs most vendors through systems, and Vendor Central relationships break at that seam.

title: Amazon held its first ad conference for brands, AdCon 2019, in Seattle
author: Kwontified
desc: Amazon held its first large advertising conference aimed at brands last week in Seattle, drawing about 400 people to a two-day, invite-only event called…

title: Lifetime value on Amazon is rented back through the ad auction
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: A repeat Amazon customer is worth what each reorder earns after the ad you may need to win it back, which is why brands misjudge lifetime value on Amazon.

title: Seller Fulfilled Prime in Q4 bets the badge on your own dock
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Choosing FBA or Seller Fulfilled Prime before Q4 decides where a holiday failure would happen, and most brands make that call on parcel rates alone.

title: Instagram Checkout fees pay off only on sales your site loses
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Instagram’s Checkout fee is charged on every in-app order, including ones your website would have closed anyway, so incremental orders set the break-even.

title: Amazon influencer storefronts move the sale to Amazon’s shelf
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: The same creator can send a follower to your Instagram checkout or to an Amazon storefront. Who pays the creator decides whose shelf the shopper lands on.

title: Mercado Libre cross-border pricing is a bet on the currency
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: A brand selling into Brazil or Argentina from the US must decide who carries the currency: its margin in dollars or its shoppers’ prices. Set a band and a rule.

title: Amazon bundles work when they finish a job, not clear a shelf
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Shoppers pay for Amazon bundles that complete a task and discount add-ons they never wanted. Each kit is a new product to run, so build few and build them well.

title: Mercado Libre Product Ads should be bid from margin, not price
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Mercado Libre Product Ads sell search position by the click. Today’s low prices reflect few bidders; set the maximum bid from what a click is worth to you.

title: Regional brands on Amazon get a national shelf, not a following
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Amazon lets a regional brand reach all 50 states without slotting fees, but shoppers outside its home market do not search for it. Plan for two audiences.

title: Sports and outdoors on Amazon in 2019 squeezes the middle brands
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Amazon’s sports and outdoors shelf is splitting into famous brands it may badge and its own cheaper labels. The brands in between need a reason to be picked.

title: Tariff landed cost on Amazon takes more price than the duty
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: A $3.00 tariff on a jacket sold on Amazon needs about $4.11 of extra price to recover, because referral fees and ad budgets take a share of every dollar added.

title: US 15% tariffs on $112 billion of Chinese imports, including most clothing, take effect
author: Kwontified
desc: A 15% tariff on about $112 billion of Chinese imports took effect on Sunday, September 1, 2019, reaching clothing, shoes and other consumer goods that…

title: For a new brand, the first five Amazon reviews replace the buyer
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: In a store, a buyer’s yes tells shoppers a new brand is worth a look. On Amazon the first five reviews do that job, and launch plans rarely budget for them.

title: Zalando Fulfillment Solutions pays for steady sellers only
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Zalando’s fulfillment service saves partner brands parcel costs and splits their stock in two. That second pool costs most on small, unpredictable styles.

title: Boards ask how big the Amazon channel is. Ask who controls it
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: A board’s Amazon slide usually shows growth. The questions that matter in 2019 are about control: of price, of supply, of ads and of the profit left over.

title: Enhanced Brand Content earns its keep in conversion rate
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Enhanced Brand Content costs nothing, but it pays only through conversion rate, which also sets what every paid click is worth. Test it with matched pairs.

title: Amazon agency or in-house: the real question is who joins it up
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Choosing an agency, a consultant or an in-house team for Amazon matters less than deciding who owns the joins between operations, ads and content.

title: A Q4 2019 budget should follow the value of a click
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Q4 2019 has six fewer days between Thanksgiving and Christmas. Phase Amazon ad budgets by what a click is worth in each week, not by the calendar.

title: Delivery promises now decide what goes in the basket
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Amazon’s one-day Prime and Walmart’s NextDay set different rules for the basket, and those rules now change which products shoppers buy online.

title: Amazon’s Q2 2019 other revenue slowed only on paper
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon’s ad-heavy other revenue grew 37% in Q2 2019. The slowdown from 2018 is an accounting base effect; ads still outgrew Amazon’s retail sales.

title: Amazon grocery in 2019 is arranged by the cost of the box
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Amazon grocery sorts products by what each order costs to deliver, so pack sizes built for a supermarket shelf often lose money in Amazon’s delivered box.

title: Amazon Sponsored Ads benchmark, Q2 2019: top of search paid off
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Top of search took 45% of Sponsored Products spend in Q2 2019 and returned over half the sales. The dearest click in the account was the cheapest sale.

title: Prime Day 2019’s rivals competed on what Amazon could not offer
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Target, Walmart and eBay ran events on Prime Day 2019 built on what Amazon lacks: no fee, stores, partner funding. Brands now face four July events, not one.

title: Amazon long-term storage fees: slow stock now costs every month
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: From September, Amazon assesses long-term storage every month, with a 50-cent monthly minimum on year-old units. Small, cheap products are hit hardest.

title: Amazon beauty in 2018: prestige brands trade supply for control
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Luxury beauty was Amazon’s fastest-growing category in 2017. Prestige brands are entering on new terms: selling to Amazon in return for control of their pages.

title: FBA or merchant-fulfilled: compare the cost per sale, not per box
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Fulfillment by Amazon often costs more per box but less per sale, because the Prime badge lifts conversion and Buy Box share. Model both before choosing.

title: The Amazon product page does every job a store used to split
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: A store splits selling across packaging, signs, staff and brochures. On Amazon the product page does all of it, on a phone, with content others can edit.

title: The Amazon Buy Box is a rule set: a gate, then a race
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: The Amazon Buy Box works in two stages: an eligibility gate, then a contest on price and fulfillment. Brands should fix the gate before they cut prices.

title: Instagram shopping tags turn a brand’s posts into a shelf
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: On Amazon shoppers search; on Instagram products find them. Tagged products turn a brand’s posts into a shelf, which changes what brands photograph and measure.

title: Instagram opens shoppable posts to businesses in eight more countries
author: Kwontified
desc: Instagram expanded shopping on Instagram, which lets businesses tag products in their posts, to the UK, France, Italy, Germany, Australia, Brazil, Canada…

title: Google Shopping Actions turns retailers into sellers in one cart
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Google’s Shopping Actions charges retailers per sale and puts them in one cart, so a brand’s products compete on price across retailers. Plan for it.

title: Google launches Shopping Actions, a shared cart for retailers across Search and Assistant
author: Kwontified
desc: Google launched Shopping Actions on March 19, 2018, a program that lets shoppers buy retailers’ products through Google Search and the Google Assistant…

title: Amazon reviews are a shared reputation built by the first five
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: The first few Amazon reviews do most of the work, they are harder to earn since 2016, and every seller on a listing shares them. Plan reviews deliberately.

title: Set Amazon ACoS targets from margin, not from a benchmark
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: A benchmark ACoS means opposite things for products with different margins. Set each Amazon ACoS target from the product’s own margin and its goal.

title: Amazon apparel in 2018 is a store, not an overflow channel
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Amazon apparel changed in 2017: forecast to pass Macy’s, it signed Nike, grew its own labels and raised clothing fees. Brands need a plan for its store.

title: Negative keywords: when to block an Amazon search, by the numbers
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Negative keywords are Amazon advertising’s cheapest efficiency gain when added by rule: block irrelevant searches at once, weak ones after enough clicks.

title: Unauthorized Amazon sellers start with a brand’s own distribution
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Most unauthorized Amazon sellers get their stock from a brand’s own wholesale, liquidation and supplier channels. The fix starts with how the brand distributes.

title: Test the Amazon Advertising Platform against a holdout group
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: The Amazon Advertising Platform reaches shoppers before and after they search, and its reports credit it with sales that would have happened anyway. Test it.

title: Amazon Vendor Central’s real price comes after the purchase order
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Amazon vendors negotiate a wholesale price, then lose part of it to co-op, allowances, chargebacks and payment terms. The real price is what remains.

title: Amazon Marketing Services only reaches shoppers already searching
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Almost all Amazon Marketing Services spending buys search ads, which capture demand that already exists. For brands, that sets a ceiling on growth from AMS.

title: Instagram shopping is free to join, but reach will not stay free
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Instagram opened shoppable posts to more US brands in 2017 and plans to charge for reaching new shoppers. For brands, 2018 is the cheap year to learn it.

title: Mercado Libre is buying its growth with free shipping
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Mercado Libre’s sales accelerated in 2017 as it paid for free shipping. For brands entering Latin America in 2018, shipping eligibility decides who wins.

title: Zalando’s Partner Program lets brands run their own shelf
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Zalando grew 23% in 2017 and is opening its platform to brands that sell their own stock. For brands in Europe, the choice is how much of the shelf to run.

title: Amazon advertising revenue grew three times faster than its store
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon’s ‘other’ revenue, mostly advertising, grew 62% in Q4 2017 as store sales grew 20%. For brands, the cost of being found is rising faster than sales.

title: Walmart Marketplace in 2018 is still early enough to shape
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Walmart’s online catalog tripled in a year as its marketplace grew faster than its own sales. For brands, 2018 is a chance to shape the shelf before it fills.

title: Amazon ad benchmarks, Q4 2017: Sponsored Products sold best
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Public Q4 2017 data shows Amazon ad spend rising fast, Headline Search Ads growing fastest and Sponsored Products earning the most sales per click.

title: Staying off Amazon does not keep a brand off Amazon
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Brands that refuse Amazon over counterfeits rarely leave it. Their products stay, sold by others, and the brand gives up its say over the page shoppers read.

title: Amazon’s 2018 fee changes cut the advertising ceiling first
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon’s 2018 fee increases lower the most a brand can spend on ads for each sale by the same amount. Model it product by product before February 22.

title: Amazon raises clothing and handbag referral fees as FBA fees rise on February 22
author: Kwontified
desc: Amazon told sellers on January 18, 2018 that it will raise referral fees for Clothing & Accessories and for Shoes, Handbags & Sunglasses from April 15…

title: NRF 2018 signaled that stores are becoming warehouses
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: NRF 2018 was optimistic about stores for a reason brands should note: retailers are turning stores into warehouses, and shoppers now choose online first.

title: Automatic campaigns are research, not an Amazon ad strategy
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: Amazon automatic campaigns find searches a brand never thought of. Left in charge of the budget, they bid one price on all of them. Harvest, then negate.

title: Vendor Central or Seller Central is an org chart decision
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: Choosing Vendor Central or Seller Central decides which team runs Amazon inside a brand. Most brands choose the channel and forget to staff it.

title: Headline Search Ads earn their cost on searches without a brand
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: The banner atop Amazon search pays for itself where shoppers have not chosen a brand. On a brand’s own name, it often buys clicks the brand already had.

title: Kwontified partners Elaine Kwon and Jordan Taylor to attend NRF 2018: Retail’s Big Show
author: Kwontified

title: Amazon Brand Registry decides who controls a brand’s listings
author: Elaine Kwon
desc: On Amazon, control of a product page follows registration, not ownership. Why brands lose listings to resellers, and how the new Brand Registry helps.

title: The Sponsored Products default bid prices every search the same
author: Jordan Taylor
desc: One default bid prices every search in an ad group the same, though searches differ in what a click is worth. Set bids per keyword from conversion value.
